binders: n is an arbitrary natural number.
x is a real vector indexed by Fin n, equivalently an n-coordinate real vector.
a is an arbitrary real scalar.
j is an arbitrary index in Fin n.
conclusions: The j-th normalized exponential coordinate is invariant under subtracting the same scalar a from every coordinate: exp(x_j-a) / Σ_{i∈Fin n} exp(x_i-a) = exp(x_j) / Σ_{i∈Fin n} exp(x_i).
The normalized exponential coordinates of x sum to one: Σ_{i∈Fin n} exp(x_i) / Σ_{k∈Fin n} exp(x_k) = 1.
The absolute values of the normalized exponential coordinates of x sum to one: Σ_{i∈Fin n} |exp(x_i) / Σ_{k∈Fin n} exp(x_k)| = 1.
mathematical_definitions: Define the common shifted vector x-a·1 by (x-a·1)_i = x_i-a.
The final sum is the finite ℓ1 norm Σ_{i∈Fin n} |S_i(x)|.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite-dimensional real vector x, every real scalar a, and every available coordinate j, subtracting a from every coordinate leaves the j-th normalized exponential coordinate unchanged. Moreover, the normalized exponential coordinates of x have total sum exactly one and total absolute-value sum exactly one.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There are no explicit hypotheses, including no stated assumption that n is positive or that an exponential denominator is nonzero.

When n = 0, Fin n has no element j, so the entire universally quantified proposition is vacuously true; in particular, the two normalization equalities are not substantively asserted for the empty vector.

In every nonvacuous instance, the binder j : Fin n forces n > 0. The positivity and nonvanishing of the exponential denominator are consequences of the definitions and standard real exponential properties, not encoded assumptions.
Real division is formally total even at denominator zero, although denominator zero cannot occur in a nonvacuous instance because the finite sum contains at least one positive exponential term.
The invariance conclusion concerns a common scalar shift applied to every coordinate, not an arbitrary coordinate-dependent perturbation.
The two sum conclusions are written only for the original vector x, not explicitly for the shifted vector.

The proposition does not explicitly state coordinatewise nonnegativity, strict positivity, upper bounds, or a separate vector-level equality, even though some such facts may follow from the definitions.
All quantities use exact real arithmetic and the exact real exponential; no floating-point computation, approximation, rounding, error bound, or algorithm is encoded.
